subject.title: [Feature]: Support plugin-requestable session isolation for trust boundaries

question: Should OpenClaw expose plugin-requestable quarantined execution as a public Plugin SDK/runtime contract, and what concrete isolation and trust-metadata guarantees should it make?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the permanent API shape would define a security boundary and public Plugin SDK expectations that automation should not choose.

options.title: Keep As Design Item
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers define isolation semantics, trust metadata, prerequisite hook context, failure behavior, and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Primitives
options.body: Defer the hook directive and document current `sessions_spawn` sandbox patterns as the supported workaround for trusted operators.

options.title: Close As Out Of Scope
options.body: Reject plugin-requestable trust-boundary execution if maintainers decide strong isolation must stay at separate gateway or OS-host boundaries.

recommendation.title: Keep As Design Item
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers define isolation semantics, trust metadata, prerequisite hook context, failure behavior, and compatibility expectations.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is recent ownership of the subagent context/thread runtime and adjacent security-sensitive hook surfaces.
